# ODM suite redesign — design

**Status:** approved by the user on 2026-11-02, including the five additions below.
**Mockups:** `design/odm-suite/odm-suite.figcraft` (FigCraft 0.14), regenerated by `python design/odm-suite/build.py`. Frame numbers below refer to it.

## Goal

Some users say ODM is hard to use. Make the everyday path obvious without taking anything away from the people who already love it: paste a link, see what ODM found, download, and always see the next step on the download itself.

The word "suite" here means the complete set of screens. The current table stays available as the Detailed view.

## Understanding

**From the request:** people like ODM, some reviews call the UX hard, the answer is a new suite, and other features and bugs wait until later.

**Assumptions to confirm:**
- The review text has not been read. The problems below come from reading the UI code, not from what users wrote.
- The new suite becomes the default for everyone, including existing users, with one click back to the Detailed view.
- Every current feature stays reachable.

**Success looks like:**
- A new user finishes these without help: add a link, pause it, find the finished file, recover from an expired link.
- A current user can reach everything they use today.
- No engine behaviour changes beyond the additions in "Queue and format additions".

## Problems this solves

| Today (code) | Effect | New suite |
|---|---|---|
| `Toolbar.svelte`: Resume, Pause, Cancel and Remove stay disabled until a row is selected | The buttons look broken to anyone who has not selected a row | Each row carries its own next step |
| `DownloadTable.svelte`: details open on double-click or Enter, with no visible cue | Details stay undiscovered | A plain click on a card opens details |
| `AddDialog.svelte`: Address plus five fields before the first download | Feels like a form to fill in | Paste, check, Download; fields sit under More options |
| `Sidebar.svelte`: 5 statuses plus 8 categories always visible | Many choices, little meaning | Five tabs and one type dropdown |
| `rowStatus`: failures show as a status word; the fix sits in the details panel | People do not know what to do next | Plain explanation and one fix button on the row |
| `WelcomeDialog.svelte`: three steps in one modal | Setup looks heavy | One step per screen |
| `settingsPage.ts`: 9 sections | Hard to scan | 6 sections, Essentials first |

## Principles

1. The next step is on the download.
2. Orange means the next step. A screen shows one orange action where it can.
3. Say it in plain words first; technical terms live behind a disclosure.
4. Nothing is removed, only moved.

## Screens

| Frame | Screen |
|---|---|
| 01, 02, 02b | Welcome: browser, connect, video tools |
| 03 | Home, first launch |
| 00 | Home with downloads |
| 04, 05, 06, 07 | Add panel: file, more options, video page, torrent |
| 08 | Details drawer |
| 09 | Problems tab |
| 10 | Detailed view with selection bar |
| 11 | Settings: Essentials |
| 12, 12b | Speed menu, row menu |
| 12c | Up next: choosing the order |
| 13 | Smallest window, 900 × 560 (`minWidth` and `minHeight` are unchanged) |

## Home

From top to bottom: header, tabs, list, status bar.

**Header.** Mark, paste bar, Add several, Settings. Both buttons keep their text labels.

**Tabs and filters.** `Filter` is one value today, so a tab and a type cannot combine. It becomes two: `status: StatusFilter` and `category: string | null`. `downloads.setFilter`, `matches`, `counts` and `visible` change to match. Tab counts respect the chosen type.

| Tab | Rows | Change from today |
|---|---|---|
| All | Every row | None |
| Downloading | `isActive(state)` | None |
| Up next | `queued`, `paused` | None |
| Finished | `completed`, `cancelled` | `cancelled` moves here from `failed` |
| Problems | `failed` | No longer includes `cancelled` |

**Cards view.** In the All tab, rows are grouped in this order: Needs you, Downloading, Up next, Finished. Empty groups are hidden. Needs you holds `failed` rows and torrents waiting for a file choice. Other tabs show a flat list. Rows inside a group keep the current sort.

**Row.** Type tile, name, one-line summary, progress bar while there is progress, then actions on the right.

| State | Summary | Actions |
|---|---|---|
| `downloading`, `probing`, `merging` | "3.1 GB of 5.9 GB · 6 min left", speed shown | Pause, `…` |
| `paused` | "Paused at 38%" | Resume, `…` |
| `queued` | `rowStatus` text, including the queue schedule's wait | Start now while the queue schedule is closed (`canResume(row, true)`), otherwise Pause; `…` |
| `paused`, waiting for a torrent file choice | `rowStatus` text | Choose files (reopens `ConfirmDialog`), `…` |
| `failed` | `problemInfo(row).summary` | Its fix button (primary), `…` |
| `completed` | Size and finish time | Open, Open folder, `…` |
| `cancelled` | "Cancelled" | Remove, `…` |

The `…` menu holds Details, Open folder, Copy link, Paste new link (when `canRefresh`), Cancel download (when `canCancel`) and Remove from list. Items that do not apply are hidden, not greyed out.

Open keeps the risky-file check (`isRiskyFile` → `OpenProgramDialog`). Start now is the same `api.resume` the toolbar uses today; ODM has no way to jump a queued row past a free slot limit, and this redesign does not add one. Remove and Cancel keep their dialogs.

**Selection.** Cards: click opens details, Ctrl+click and Shift+click select. Detailed view: selection behaves as it does today. In both, a floating selection bar shows the count and the actions from `canPause`, `canResume` and `canCancel`, plus Remove. The bar replaces the toolbar buttons.

**Status bar.** Browser status (opens `BrowserDialog`), update notice, remaining queue size, total speed and speed limit. The speed limit control is `SpeedChip` moved here; its menu opens upward with the same presets, Custom and Pause all or Resume all. `UpdateBanner` becomes the update notice. The `downloads.error` banner stays where it is.

**View toggle.** New persisted setting `list_view: "cards" | "table"`, default `cards`, with a `Settings::from_json` default so existing files load. `table` shows `DownloadTable` in the new chrome.

## Add panel

`AddDialog` becomes a panel attached to the paste bar. Its logic stays: `suggest` debounce, `isMagnet`, `waits`, `limitError`, `add`, `addTorrent`.

**Opening.** Pasting into the bar, Ctrl+V anywhere outside a text field, or Ctrl+N (which focuses the bar). The `paste` event on the window supplies the text, so no new permission is needed. Text that is not an address or magnet is ignored outside the bar.

**Default content.** Preview (name, facts from `suggest`) and destination with Change. The primary label keeps today's rules: "Download", "Add paused" or "Add to queue", with Start now when `waits` is true.

**More options.** File name, Save to, Type, Connections, Speed limit. Shown fields follow today's rules (`plainFile`, `is_page`).

**Video page.** The quality chips and subtitles checkbox from frame 06 default to Settings and use `VideoOverride` (see "Queue and format additions"). Sizes per quality are not shown, because ODM does not know them before downloading. HLS shows its existing `variants` list as chips.

**Torrents.** The row is created first and `ConfirmDialog` asks for files, as today. `ConfirmDialog` takes the panel layout for both torrents and "Ask where to save each one". Cancel behaves as it does today.

**Torrent file.** The Torrents card on the first-launch screen and a line under the focused empty paste bar both open `pickTorrentFile`. Dropping a `.torrent` on the window still works. Frames 03 and 07 show the card and the file list; the line under the bar is not mocked.

## Details drawer

`DetailPanel` keeps its data and effects, and becomes a 400 px drawer over the list. Esc or the close button dismisses it.

From top to bottom: name; percent and bar; Speed and Time left; primary action, Open folder, Copy link, Remove; Saved to; Speed limit. Below a closed "Technical details" disclosure: chunk or piece map, connections, address, redirect, headers, info hash and the raw error message. Peers, Uploading and the torrent file list stay in the main section for torrents, because they are what torrent users look for.

`needsVideoTools` keeps showing `ToolsCard`, now from the row's fix button as well.

## Problems

New pure function `problemInfo(row): { title, summary, body, action }` in `model.ts`, keyed on `error_code`, which is already structured. `needsVideoTools(error_message)` is checked first. The raw `error_message` stays under Technical details.

| Code | Title | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `link_expired` | The download link expired | Paste new link |
| yt-dlp or FFmpeg missing | This video needs the video tools | Install |
| `disk_full` | Not enough disk space | Try again |
| `permission_denied` | ODM can't save to this folder | Try again |
| `timeout`, `connection`, `dns`, `http_408`, `http_429`, `http_5xx` | The server stopped responding | Try again |
| Other `http_*` | The server refused this download | Paste new link |
| `file_changed` | The file changed on the server | Paste new link |
| `checksum_mismatch` | The file arrived damaged | Try again |
| `range_ignored`, `io`, `other`, none | The download stopped | Try again |

"Your progress is safe" appears only for `link_expired`, the case `RefreshUrlDialog` promises to continue. Paste new link opens `RefreshUrlDialog`, retitled to match. Try again is `api.resume`. Free space is not shown: ODM has no lookup for it.

## Welcome

`WelcomeDialog` becomes a full-window flow, one step per screen, with its logic unchanged: `integration` polling, `storeLinkFor`, the Firefox branch, `ToolsCard`, and `finish` setting `onboarding_done`.

- Frame 02 shows the manual path, which is today's real path. When `storeLink` exists, the step is a single "Add to {browser}" button.
- The step moves on by itself when `browserConnected` turns true.
- Skip setup and Do this later both call `finish`.
- Linux keeps its own size wording (`IS_LINUX`).
- `BrowserDialog`'s `onsetup` still opens this flow.

## Settings

`SECTIONS` goes from 9 to 6. Every setting stays, search still covers all of them, and `onOpenSettings` keeps old section ids working through an alias map.

| New section | Holds |
|---|---|
| Essentials (new) | Download folder, sort by type, downloads at once, speed limit, notify when finished, keep running in tray, check for updates |
| Downloads | Downloads and Speed, including both schedules |
| Browser | Unchanged |
| Video | Unchanged |
| Torrents | Unchanged |
| Advanced | Network, Advanced, and what remains of General and Updates |

Essentials controls edit the same settings keys as their home sections, so nothing is stored twice. Search lists each setting once, under its home section.

## Dialogs that stay

`BatchDialog`, `RemoveDialog`, `CancelDialog`, `ExistsDialog`, `ReuseDialog`, `AfterQueueDialog`, `OpenProgramDialog` and `BrowserDialog` keep their content and pick up the new tokens.

## Foundations

**Colour.** `app.css` names and values stay. Rule change: orange marks the next step only, so the active tab uses `--surface-2`, not orange. `--idle` stays non-text.

**Radius.** `--radius` 7px (controls), `--radius-lg` 10px (rows, cards, pills), new `--radius-xl` 12px (panels).

**Type.** Inter, bundled as a variable `woff2` under `app/src/assets/fonts/` with its OFL licence. The current CSP (`font-src 'self'`) allows it. The size added to the installer is measured in phase 1 and reported in the release notes. Numbers use tabular figures.

| Use | Size and weight |
|---|---|
| Screen title | 28 Bold |
| Section title | 22 Bold |
| Card title | 15 Semi Bold |
| Row name | 14 Semi Bold |
| Body and controls | 13 Regular |
| Summary, metadata | 12 Regular |

**Icons.** New `Icon.svelte`, using the 24-grid paths in `build.py`. Inline SVG, stroke `currentColor`.

## Queue and format additions

**Queue order.** Rows in Up next show a drag handle, and the `…` menu gains Move to top, Move up and Move down (frame 12c). The summary says "2nd in line". A new `reorder_queue(ids)` command takes the whole Up next list, top first, and writes `priority` descending, so the last row gets 1. New downloads stay at 0, so they join the end. The scheduler already reads `priority DESC, created_at ASC`, so it needs no change. Sort by size in the Up next header reorders the whole queue once, smallest first; clicking it again gives largest first. Rows with no known size go last. The result is saved like a manual order, and dragging afterwards still works. Order decides what starts next and never stops a running download. Up next sorts by priority in both views, ignoring the table's sort key.

**Total size.** New pure function `remaining(rows): { bytes, unknown }` over rows in `isActive` states plus `queued` and `paused`. It sums `size - bytes` and counts rows with no size. Failed, finished and cancelled rows do not count. The status bar shows "3.7 GB left" or "3.7 GB + 2 unknown left", and hides when nothing is left. Group headers show their own figure, as frames 00 and 12c do.

**Video bar.** The bar moves by dragging its handle, keeps its place in `storage.local` across sites, and stays on screen when the window shrinks. Its × still hides it for the page. The hover button gains a × that hides it for the page. Per-site off in the popup is unchanged. The drag handle is reachable by keyboard: arrow keys move the bar by 16 px.

**MP3 and MP4.** Each detected video offers video and MP3 in the hover button, the on-page list and the popup. Site videos and HLS say MP4. A plain file says its own extension, such as WEBM, because ODM does not convert video.

`VideoOverride { quality, container, subtitles }`, all optional, is stored as JSON in a new nullable `video_override` column, so a choice survives pause, resume and restart. No override means Settings apply. MP3 is `quality: audio`. Site videos use yt-dlp's existing `-x --audio-format mp3`. Plain files and HLS finish, then FFmpeg converts them with `-vn -c:a libmp3lame -q:a 2`, keeping state `merging`. Without FFmpeg the download fails with the existing "FFmpeg not found" wording, so the video tools fix appears. If conversion fails, the downloaded file stays.

**Vivaldi on Linux.** When ODM does not answer, the extension shows the error badge and keeps the last error for the popup. The cause is traced separately, starting in WSL.

## Keyboard and accessibility

- Kept: Ctrl+Shift+N, Ctrl+, , Delete, Esc. Ctrl+N now focuses the paste bar.
- New: Ctrl+V outside text fields.
- Cards are focusable. Enter opens details, Space toggles selection.
- Row buttons name their file, for example "Pause ubuntu-24.04-desktop-amd64.iso".
- Tabs use `tablist`. The drawer and panel trap and restore focus as `Modal` does. Status is always text, never colour alone.
- Reduced motion and `forced-colors` rules from `app.css` carry over. Cards get no selection or hover animation, matching the rule for high-frequency actions.

## Responsive behaviour

Below 1000 px of list width, the right side of the row narrows and the type dropdown stays. At the 900 px minimum (frame 13), rows keep their name, summary, bar and actions. Detailed view keeps its container-query column rules.

## Phases

1. **Foundations:** font, radius tokens, `Icon.svelte`.
2. **Home:** filter model, cards, groups, status bar, selection bar, view toggle.
3. **Add panel:** panel, Ctrl+V, `ConfirmDialog` layout.
4. **Details and problems:** drawer, `problemInfo`, row fix buttons.
5. **Welcome.**
6. **Settings.**

Queue order and total size land in phase 2. Frame 06's chips land in phase 3 and use `VideoOverride`.

**Before phase 1:** the extension work (video bar, error badge, MP3 and MP4), which ships on its own. See `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-02-odm-extension-and-formats.md`.

The suite is planned in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-02-odm-suite.md`. It lands on one branch and ships as one release, so users never see a half-new app.

## Testing

- **Vitest**, in the existing `app/src/lib/*.test.ts` style: `matches` and `counts` with the new tab mapping and two-part filter; grouping; `problemInfo` for every code in the table, including unknown codes; row action selection per state; settings section aliases.
- **Rust:** `list_view` default and round trip; `reorder_queue`; `VideoOverride` wins over Settings and survives a restart.
- **Checks:** `pnpm check`, `pnpm test`, `cargo test`.
- **By hand, on Windows and Linux:** a smoke pass of file, HLS, site video, magnet and `.torrent`, plus keyboard-only use of home and the add panel.
- **People:** before release, watch at least three people who have not used ODM do the four tasks in "Success looks like".

## Out of scope

Light theme, restyling the browser extension beyond the additions above, the website, and download features not listed here. The `.figcraft` file is a reference, not a source of generated code.

## Open question

The review text should be read before phase 2. If reviews point somewhere else, such as extension setup, the order of phases changes.
